annotation.title_clean: Evolving Skill Modules under a Fixed Planner: Versioning, Rollback, and Runtime Governance for Long-Lived Robot Systems
annotation.title_en: Evolving Skill Modules under a Fixed Planner: Versioning, Rollback, and Runtime Governance for Long-Lived Robot Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Qin, X.; Luan, S.; Yang, C.; Li, Z.
annotation.venue: arXiv (preprint submitted to Journal of Systems and Software)
annotation.summary_en: Robotics software-engineering preprint on versioning, promotion gating, rollback and a runtime action shield for continually retrained robot skill modules, tested on six robosuite tasks. It reports negative results (unstable seeds, modules were whole-task policies, shield blocked all success) and that a promotion gate rejected all injected regressions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Peak task success varies widely across seeds (23.3 to 73.3%), so single-run peaks cannot rank methods.
The four 'modules' were whole-task policies rotated on a clock, not a phase decomposition; retention was 0.734 versus 0.023 for the rotation.
The runtime shield cut violations 98-100% on five tasks but left success at zero, because its acceptance criterion omitted task completions.
A promotion gate rejected all twelve injected regressions, at a 22.5% cost in rejected clean candidates.
A dip detector with rollback caught nine of twelve regressions and missed all three on one seed.
